title: The Vanishing Record
verdict: Ada Hayes was responsible for the disappearance of a guest-room master key.
intent: Ada Hayes wanted to enter a guest room and remove an incriminating photograph.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the ski instructor crossed between the fireplace room and the mudroom to check equipment.
Remove a guest-room master key from its checked location.
Hide the item in a hollow ski pole standing in the mudroom rack.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a guest-room master key disappeared from a mountain lodge after a snowstorm.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the mudroom bell rang while everyone claimed to be indoors.
The physical trace was dry snow under only one chair near the mudroom.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a wax scraper with fresh brass scratches.
The item could be concealed in a hollow ski pole standing in the mudroom rack.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the ski instructor knew the pole cap unscrewed silently.
distractor_cues: a housekeeper seen near the linen closet
a guide carrying a bulky parka
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
